title: What If a Hurricane Had 500 MPH Winds? Meet the Hypercane

scenes.text: What if a hurricane had winds of 500 miles an hour? Scientists calculated it could exist.
It's called a hypercane, and it needs ocean water near 50 degrees Celsius. That's 12 degrees above any sea on record.
Ordinary hurricanes top out near 200 miles an hour. A hypercane would reach about 500.
Its clouds would climb 30 to 40 kilometers, far above airliners, into the stratosphere.
scenes.keywords: storm clouds from airplane high altitude

scenes.text: It would last at least several weeks, shrinking into a tight core as it strengthened.
None has ever been seen. Scientists think only a giant impact could heat that much sea, and it may have added to the dinosaurs' end.

description:
What if a hurricane had winds of 500 miles an hour?
MIT scientist Kerry Emanuel calculated that a hypercane could form over water near 50 degrees Celsius, and its clouds would reach the stratosphere.
What should we run through next?
